goes-r-databook.title: GOES-R Series Data Book, Revision A
goes-r-databook.publisher: NASA GOES-R Series Program / NOAA OSPO
goes-r-databook.quote: The LWIR and MWIR optics and FPMs are maintained at approximately 60K.
goes-r-databook.note: Downloaded directly; all cited pages visually inspected. The seed aperture claim was not found. System raw and rebroadcast link rates are not ABI detector rates.

noaa-abi-page.title: Advanced Baseline Imager (ABI)
noaa-abi-page.quote: It detects visible and infrared light using 16 spectral bands, with each band capturing a different set of data.

landsat9-tirs2-nasa.title: Thermal Infrared Sensor (TIRS)
landsat9-tirs2-nasa.quote: TIRS employs Quantum Well Infrared Photodetectors (QWIPs) to detect long wavelengths of light
landsat9-tirs2-nasa.note: This shared page mixes Landsat 8 and 9, and its 640-detector image caption explicitly names Landsat 8. Dedicated TIRS-2 sources below corroborate L9 facts.

nasa-tirs2-build.title: TIRS-2 Testing: A Landsat 9 Instrument Takes Shape
nasa-tirs2-build.section: Instrument design paragraphs following test photographs
nasa-tirs2-build.quote: A two-stage mechanical cryocooler will cool TIRS-2’s focal plane.
nasa-tirs2-build.note: Historical prelaunch design article; its anticipated launch date is not a current schedule claim.

nasa-tirs2-spectral.title: Landsat 9 Thermal Infrared Sensor 2 Subsystem-Level Spectral Test Results
nasa-tirs2-spectral.quote: The three SCAs (SCA-A, B, and C) have 640 × 512 pixels each
nasa-tirs2-spectral.note: Science mode combines two rows per channel into one effective row; do not compute data rate from every physical array element. Source labels the second channel B12 inconsistently; use NASA's shared-page Bands 10 and 11 designation.

nasa-irdetectors-ntrs.title: Infrared Detectors Overview in the Short Wave Infrared to Far Infrared for CLARREO Mission
nasa-irdetectors-ntrs.dated: 2010 (PDF creation metadata; exact publication date unconfirmed)
nasa-irdetectors-ntrs.section: PDF pp. 3-7, sections A.1-A.3 and Table 1
nasa-irdetectors-ntrs.quote: The dual band InSb/HgCdTe sandwich detector operates at 77°K
nasa-irdetectors-ntrs.note: Material names do not define universal operating temperatures. Values in this review are tied to specific civil instruments or laboratory devices. AIRS prose and Table 1 differ (60 K vs. 58 K); omit a single AIRS value. T2SL default remains unresolved.

nist-cryocooler-2009.title: Cryocoolers: the state of the art and recent developments
nist-cryocooler-2009.quote: Efficiencies at 80 K can be as high as about 20% of Carnot for some of the best space cryocoolers
nist-cryocooler-2009.note: A dated review, not a specification for ABI, TIRS-2, or any military instrument.

nist-refrigeration-2020.title: Review of Refrigeration Methods (submitted chapter)
nist-refrigeration-2020.section: PDF pp. 2-3, equation (1) and following paragraph
nist-refrigeration-2020.quote: The actual COP of a real refrigerator can be expressed as a percentage of the Carnot COP
nist-refrigeration-2020.note: Equation (1): COP_Carnot = Tc / (Th - Tc). Any future heat lift, hot temperature, or efficiency selected for the schematic remains Assumed. No engine implementation in Phase 1.

nasa-combustion-bands.title: Determination of primary-zone smoke concentrations from spectral radiance measurements in gas turbine combustors
nasa-combustion-bands.section: Printed p. 5; PDF p. 7, gaseous combustion products paragraph
nasa-combustion-bands.quote: they absorb and emit radiation only within discrete wavelengths.
nasa-combustion-bands.note: Use only general molecular-band physics. This civil gas-turbine source establishes H2O and CO2 emission bands, not a rocket intensity, temperature, atmospheric transmission model, or real sensor response.

nasa-atmospheric-windows.title: Remote Sensing
nasa-atmospheric-windows.quote: The gases that comprise our atmosphere absorb radiation in certain wavelengths while allowing radiation with differing wavelengths to pass through.
nasa-atmospheric-windows.note: Use the qualitative definition only; no quantitative transmission or altitude-dependent claim was verified.

nasa-orbit-catalog.title: Catalog of Earth Satellite Orbits
nasa-orbit-catalog.section: High Earth Orbit; Medium Earth Orbit
nasa-orbit-catalog.quote: A satellite in a circular geosynchronous orbit directly over the equator (eccentricity and inclination at zero) will have a geostationary orbit
nasa-orbit-catalog.note: General orbit definitions only. Historical mission examples in this article are not current status. Molniya values describe a generic orbit, not actual warning-satellite elements.

noaa-geo-definition.title: Geostationary Earth Orbit Satellite (GEO)
noaa-geo-definition.quote: 35,786 kilometers above the Equator, rotating with the Earth as both move through space.
